According to recent reports, if you need some new tools for your holiday DIY projects, or if you have a DIYer on your list, Black Friday deals are one of the best ways to save money on tools. DeWalt has been making cordless tools for over 30 years, and they have a reputation for making durable, reliable tools. Here are the best Early Black Friday deals on DeWalt cordless tools.

A good quality drill and driver is the foundation of a home tool set because they allow you to drive screws and bolts and drill pilot holes for basic projects like putting up shelves, as well as more advanced woodworking and maintenance tasks.

The DeWalt 20-volt MAX drill and driver set is on sale on Amazon for $129, 46% off its regular price. The set comes with a drill, an impact driver, two 1.5-amp-hour batteries, a charger, and a tool bag. This is a good starter set because it has everything you need to use it right out of the box.

The DeWalt 20-volt compact drill is on sale at Home Depot for $99, 45% off its usual price. It comes with a 20-volt, 2-amp-hour battery and a charger. This is the first basic cordless tool you need for most DIY home maintenance.

It has been revealed that the DeWalt 20-volt compact impact driver is on sale at Home Depot for $99, 45% off its usual price. It comes with a 2-amp-hour battery and a charger. This is a good tool for an expanding home tool set, allowing you to drive screws and bolts into tougher materials with less effort.

Recent findings suggest that saws and trimming tools are a key part of a compact tool set if you strategy to cut and shape your materials. They can be useful for DIY projects from fence repair to installing custom trim.

According to recent reports, the DeWalt 60-volt Flex 7 ¼-inch circular saw is on sale at Home Depot for $299, 52% off its regular price. This saw comes with a 60-20-volt Flex 12-amp-hour battery. You’ll need a charger for the high-capacity battery. This is a good saw for working farther away from a power source because the battery is designed for longer run-time between charges.

In a recent development, the DeWalt 20-volt MAX cordless jigsaw and the DeWalt 20-volt MAX cordless router are on sale at Home Depot for $199 at Home Depot, 60% off its usual price. They come with a 4-amp-hour battery, a 6-amp-hour battery, and a charger. These are woodworking tools that can be used to shape trim and make specialty cuts.

According to recent reports, the DeWalt 60-volt Flex compact cordless angle grinder is on sale at Home Depot for $299, 51% off its typical price. This tool comes with a 20-60-volt battery. You’ll need a charger for the high-capacity battery. This is a good tool for metalworking or for grinding off screw and nail tips if they poke through your material.

The DeWalt 20-volt oscillating multi-tool set is on sale for $99, 50% off its regular price. This set comes with the oscillating multitool, a 2-amp-hour battery, and sanding attachment and accessory wrench, and four sheets of sandpaper. This is a versatile tool that can be used for cutting and finishing projects.

Batteries are one of the most expensive parts of a cordless tool set, and having a few extras so you can always have a fresh battery on the charger to swap out helps keep your DIY projects moving.

A two-pack of DeWalt 20-volt MAX 2-amp-hour batteries is on sale at Home Depot for $79, 53% off its regular price.

A set of two DeWalt 20-volt MAX batteries and two 20-volt MAX 4-amp-hour batteries is on sale for $199, 45% off its typical price.

Yes, Home Depot has already rolled out its early Black Friday deals, offering deep discounts on major brands of cordless power tools. They also enhancement their sales page on Thanksgiving day and include Black Friday in-store-only doorbusters as part of their seasonal sales.

Home Depot and Lowe’s often compete with each other for seasonal sales, so it’s always a good idea to check both sites before buying. Right now, Home Depot has the best deals on DeWalt and Milwaukee cordless tool sets, but Lowe’s has a better deal on Craftsman hand tool sets.

The best prices of the year on tools are during the holidays in November and December. This is because of the holiday shopping push, as well as making space for fresh tools that come out in the spring. The second-best time to buy tools is in May and June during Father’s Day sales.

Report: iPhone set to gain market share in 2027 amid industry-wide slump

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (565 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple could see iPhone shipments rise 7% next year, giving it a 26% share of global smartphone shipments, according to a newly introduced report.
  • As detailed by AppleInsider, a latest Morgan Stanley research report says Apple is poised to ship approximately 270 million iPhones in 2027, a 7% bump from 2026.
  • The forecast comes amid a change of pace for Apple, which introduced only the iPhone 18 Pro models and iPhone Duo this fall, with the rest of its iPhone lineup reportedly set to arrive early next year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple could see iPhone shipments rise 7% next year, giving it a 26% share of global smartphone shipments, according to a newly introduced report. Here are the details.

As detailed by AppleInsider, a latest Morgan Stanley research report says Apple is poised to ship approximately 270 million iPhones in 2027, a 7% bump from 2026.

The forecast comes amid a change of pace for Apple, which introduced only the iPhone 18 Pro models and iPhone Duo this fall, with the rest of its iPhone lineup reportedly set to arrive early next year.

Morgan Stanley notes that this could push some purchases from late 2026 into 2027, contributing to the projected shipment growth without necessarily reflecting an increase in underlying demand.

The report also comes as Apple and the rest of the smartphone industry continue to grapple with rising memory and storage prices, though previous reports have suggested that Apple is better positioned than many of its competitors to absorb those costs.

Apple raised iPhone prices in September, after keeping them stable for much of the year while competitors had already introduced price hikes. In some cases, they raised prices more than once within a matter of months.

It has been revealed that back to the report, it notes that global smartphone shipments are expected to drop 5% next year, compared with a previous forecast of 3.6% growth. That noted, it’s still an improvement over the estimated 13.8% decline in 2026.

Industry observers note that when it comes to Apple and the iPhone specifically, Morgan Stanley notes that consumer interest in upgrading has remained largely unchanged year over year, with 37% of iPhone owners saying they are extremely likely to upgrade within the next 12 months. That’s compared with 41% of smartphone owners overall, a figure that dropped by 2 percentage points year over year.

As for the market’s reaction to the iPhone Duo, Morgan Stanley found that 22% of non-iPhone consumers surveyed expressed interest in switching to Apple’s foldable device, with that figure reaching 34% in China.

Importantly, Morgan Stanley’s survey was conducted after the iPhone Duo was announced, but before it launched, so these figures reflect consumer interest rather than actual purchasing behavior.

Apple Intelligence was another factor examined in the survey, with Morgan Stanley concluding that AI features are becoming less important in driving iPhone upgrades, while factors such as battery life and upgrade eligibility are gaining importance.

Finally, Morgan Stanley found that Apple’s customer retention rate increased three percentage points to a record 93%, while its net switching rate improved to 12%.

Huawei was the only other major smartphone brand to show a positive and improving net switching rate, while Samsung and Google remained relatively neutral, and Xiaomi, Motorola, Honor, Oppo, and Vivo recorded negative rates.

Sources indicate that why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

The Saucony Endorphin Speed has been one of the most influential running shoes of recent years, setting the template for fast training sneakers that uses some of the materials and tech from top carbon plate racers.

With the line proving so successful, Saucony has been reluctant to change much about the shoe over the five generations to date, and even though the Endorphin Speed 6 is the biggest enhancement yet thanks to a latest midsole foam, it mostly retains the same ride feel as past models.

I’ve reviewed every model of the Endorphin Speed and I’ve always been a big fan. While that’s still true with the Speed 6, this category contains some of the best running shoes available, and there are some lighter, bouncier fast trainers I rate very highly, like the New Balance SC Rebel v1 and Dynafish Xiaonian.

The Saucony Endorphin Speed 6 costs $180 in the U.S. and £180 in the U.K., which is a $5 price rise on the Endorphin Speed 5. It’s an expensive shoe, though not out of line with other plated trainers like the Hoka Mach X3 and New Balance SC Rebel v1.

Right now the Saucony Endorphin Speed 5 is widely reduced, dropping to $104 on Amazon in the Black Friday sales, which is a factor to consider when weighing up buying the Speed.

The Endorphin Speed 6 is right now available in five colors in the women’s shoe, and four colors in the men’s, including the white and yellow design I tested.

There is a wide version of the shoe available, though I found that the standard one fit me well in my normal running shoe size, the same size I’ve used with all past models of the shoe.

Saucony has added 2mm of foam to the midsole of the Endorphin Speed 6, which has a stack height of 38mm at the heel and 30mm at the forefoot, maintaining the 8mm drop of past models.

It weighs in at 8.5oz, which is 0.5oz lighter than the Endorphin Speed 5 in my size, a welcome drop for a speed-focused shoe.

The Endorphin Speed 6 has a simple mesh upper that has a little bit of padding around the tongue and collar, but mostly focuses on being lightweight and breathable.

It’s my preferred kind of upper on any shoe, since it’s not oppressively padded on the tongue or overly stiff around the heel, and I found the fit comfortable and secure throughout all my runs.

The Endorphin Speed 6’s main changes are in the midsole, which is made from a upcoming foam called PWRRUN PBX, which is meant to be lighter and bouncier than the PWRRUN PB that has been used on all past models of the shoe.

There’s also the higher stack and a redesigned nylon plate in the midsole, which aims to create a smoother, faster ride, with the Speedroll rocker on the shoe also contributing to this.

The changes to the midsole are noticeable on the run, though not as dramatically as I expected when looking at the spec sheet for the Speed 6.

Rubber is used sparingly on the bottom of the Speed 6 to keep the weight down, but patches cover the forefoot and heel of the shoe, and in my experience Saucony’s pelletized midsole foams are durable even when the foam is exposed on the bottom of a shoe.

Grip hasn’t always been a positive feature on the Speed line, but the Speed 6 provided me with reliable traction in wet conditions on both the road and the track during my testing.

After the very pleasant surprise of the original Endorphin Speed, which I ran over 300 miles in, I’ve found that the line has delivered a reliably similar experience with all of the models since.

There have been updates to make it more stable and comfortable, but ultimately all five versions of the Speed to date have had a smooth, fast and versatile ride feel.

This is still true of the Endorphin Speed 6 for me, and while that’s mostly a positive in that it performed well across a variety of runs in my testing, some might have hoped for a bigger change to challenge rivals like the SC Rebel v1 and cheaper, lighter options like the Adidas Adizero Evo SL and Dynafish Xiaonian.

I used the shoe for a couple of easy runs, two progression runs moving from easy to tempo pace, and a threshold track workout running 4 x 8min reps, and it felt great throughout.

I used the shoe for a couple of easy runs, two progression runs moving from easy to tempo pace, and a threshold track workout running 4 x 8min reps, and it felt great throughout.

The rockered midsole pushes you smoothly through your footstrike, and while the midsole foam isn’t as soft and springy as some, it does give a good amount of energy return off the toes.

In a recent development, I also found the Speed 6 to be quite stable and comfortable for easy runs, which is not always the case with plated trainers like this. I could happily use it for pretty much any kind of run, though it’s not as fast as a true carbon plate racer, or as comfortable as a max-cushioned cruiser.

To compare it directly to the Endorphin Speed 5 I did a short run wearing both shoes, and while the Speed 6 is a little bouncier and more comfortable, especially under the forefoot, I still felt the two shoes had a similar ride feel.

The Speed 6 is still a bit firmer than most super-trainers, and not as comfortable as more cushioned shoes under the toes. Some will like this more direct ride feel, but I appreciate the extra softness and bounce of a shoe like the SC Rebel v1.

Sources indicate that if you’re a long term fan of the Endorphin Speed line the Speed 6 will be a winner. It’s a mild improvement on the previous models with extra cushion and bounce, and delivers the versatile performance you expect from the line.

There is certainly a case for getting the Speed 5 instead in sales in my opinion, but the Speed 6 is a slightly better shoe overall and a successful revision.

The Speed line has been faced with increasingly fierce competition in recent years, and I don’t think the Speed 6 does much to change the equation on this front.

If you want a lighter, bouncier fast trainer, the New Balance SC Rebel v1 would be my pick, while plate-free shoes like the Adidas Evo SL, Dyanfish Xiaonian and the new 361° Mega 3 Pro all offer fast, fun rides at a lower price.

Recent findings suggest that as someone who would always have had the Endorphin Speed in my own rotation through the first few models, I’ve now moved on to shoes like this myself. Even though the Speed 6 is just as good as past models, I personally like the springier ride available in fast trainers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bowen Yang has issued an apology for calling Regina Spektor an antisemitic slur on his “Las Culturistas” podcast, saying he was unaware of the word’s origins.

“I want to genuinely apologize for using a word on the podcast without knowing its antisemitic history, especially since we’ve repudiated antisemitism on the show as recently as the last two weeks,” Yang wrote in an Instagram statement Friday. “Particularly upsetting to realize that I adopted language popularized by far-right movements whose rhetoric we should be wary of and act against.”.

“At the same time, Free Palestine,” the comedian added in a follow-up Instagram Story.

Yang drew backlash this week when a clip of an October episode of his podcast with Matt Rogers began circulating on social media. Featuring guest, actress and comedian Edy Modica, the conversation turned to Spektor, and the trio wondered what the “Samson” singer has been up to since the release of her 2022 album Home, Before and After.

Modica remarked that Spektor had been “just, like, a little Israel hardcore,” referring to Spektor’s vocal pro-Israel advocacy. Yang added, “yeah, she’s Zio.”.

Short for Zionist, the derogatory term was popularized by Ku Klux Klan leader David Duke in the early 2000s and has been picked up by white supremacist groups.

It has been revealed that the Anti-Defamation League recognizes the word as a hostile phrase when referring to Jewish people or Israelis. In response to Yang’s apology, Jonathan Greenblatt, the ADL’s CEO and National Director, slammed the comedian, saying it was “a textbook example of normalizing antisemitism.” Trending Stories Marlon Jackson Reveals Stage 4 Prostate Cancer Diagnosis Some Gamers Are Pissed That ‘GTA VI’ Makes Them Be Nice to Their Girlfriend Selena Gomez Shares Her Reaction to Martin Short Ruining Her Wedding Cake Trump Got Played by Putin and Xi.

“Apologizing for your antisemitism with not one, but two qualifications isn’t an apology at all,” Greenblatt wrote in part.

This post was updated on Friday, Nov. 20 at 4:30 p.m. to include a statement from the ADL’s Jonathan Greenblatt.

WhatsApp’s first-party chat history backup service moves ahead

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that select WhatsApp beta testers on iOS are now seeing an option to use the app’s own backup service as an alternative to iCloud.
  • A few months ago, WABetaInfo reported that WhatsApp was working on its own backup service as an alternative to the current method of backing up chats, which relies on Apple’s iCloud.
  • At the time, the feature wasn’t available even to beta testers, but WABetaInfo’s report provided details on how it would work, including 2GB of free storage, optional paid plans for larger backups, and mandatory end-to-end encryption for backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that select WhatsApp beta testers on iOS are now seeing an option to use the app’s own backup service as an alternative to iCloud. Here are the details.

A few months ago, WABetaInfo reported that WhatsApp was working on its own backup service as an alternative to the current method of backing up chats, which relies on Apple’s iCloud.

At the time, the feature wasn’t available even to beta testers, but WABetaInfo’s report provided details on how it would work, including 2GB of free storage, optional paid plans for larger backups, and mandatory end-to-end encryption for backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers.

Now, the site reports that some WhatsApp owners running the latest TestFlight build are seeing the option to switch from iCloud to WhatsApp’s own backup service, suggesting that a wider rollout may not be too far off.

People can switch to WhatsApp cloud storage from the Chat backup screen. Here, users will have to choose the backup provider they want to use. If they choose WhatsApp, they will have to secure their backups using end-to-end encryption. Since encryption is mandatory, users cannot skip this step. However, they can choose a different method to encrypt their backups. For example, users can secure their backups using a 64-digit encryption key. Users who do not know what to choose can opt for the passkey, which is the default method WhatsApp recommends. After users complete the setup, they can back up their chat history on WhatsApp’s servers. WhatsApp keeps the backup on its servers for four months after a subscription expires. If users do not renew their subscription, WhatsApp deletes the backup permanently.

Importantly, the site notes that backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers cannot right now be used to restore chats across platforms, meaning users switching from iPhone to Android, or vice versa, will still need to rely on WhatsApp’s built-in chat transfer feature.

Although the feature appears to be rolling out to beta testers first, the report notes that “the latest version available on the App Store is also compatible with this functionality,” meaning WhatsApp could theoretically enable it for customers running the public version without requiring another app update.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lauren Neustadter, President of Film & Television at Hello Sunshine, is leaving Reese Witherspoon’s organization after nearly a decade.

Industry observers note that that's where the iPad A16 comes in. This is Apple's least expensive tablet, with an MSRP of $449. But despite being Apple's "budget" option, the iPad A16 shouldn't be ignored by customers looking for the best all-around device. In fact, it's really the best iPad for most people, which is why I named it the best tablet gift of 2026. What's more, retailers are giving the iPad A16 a $50 discount ahead of Black Friday, bringing the entry-level price down to $399.

Recent findings suggest that the iPad A16 isn't Apple's best iPad (that would be the iPad Pro). It doesn't have the best display, the best camera, or the best processor. But it doesn't need those things: This iPad has a display, camera, and processor that are good enough for most use cases, without unnecessarily driving up the price. Simply put, it's one of the best tablets you can buy right now.

The iPad A16 has a large, 11-inch (technically 10.86 inches, according to Apple's fine print) IPS display with a brightness of 500 nits. As the name implies, it has Apple's A16 chip, the same processor as the iPhone 14 Pro and iPhone 15. That chip is about four years old at this point, and while that means it won't be as fast as Apple's newer SoCs, it still holds its own with iOS 27. It comes with two cameras: One 12MP wide camera on the back, with support for 4K video recording, and a 12MP Center Stage camera on the front.

According to recent reports, apple says this iPad can run for 10 hours while browsing the internet on wifi or watching video. You charge the tablet with USB-C, which supports data transfer up to USB 2.0 (which nets you 480Mb/s transfer speeds). It also comes with other perks you might expect from Apple's more "pro" tablets. You can connect the iPad to an external display, up to 4K resolution at 60Hz. It also supports two Apple Pencil models: The USB-C Apple Pencil and the first-gen Apple Pencil.

Recent findings suggest that the only real consideration here is storage: This model comes with 128GB of storage, which can run out fast. It's particularly usable for people who rely on cloud storage or mostly stream their entertainment. But if your giftee looks to store photos, videos, or music on their iPad, it's worth considering upgrading. The $50 discount applies to most storage models, as well as the cellular iPad options, except for the 512GB models: The wifi-only model has a smaller discount, while the cellular option has a $100 discount.

Sure, the iPad A16 doesn't have the fastest processor, an OLED display, support for newer accessories, or Apple's sharpest cameras. But all of the specs it does have are enough to run the things you need on iPadOS. If someone on your list is looking for an iPad for web browsing, streaming, messaging, and light gaming—and they don't need something for professional work—this device is likely more than enough iPad for them.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, iFixit’s teardown of the new Apple HomeView is now up, revealing a device that seems nearly impossible to take apart and repair.
  • Following last week’s launch of the Apple HomeView, iFixit today published its teardown of the device.
  • Contrary to recent teardowns, which found significant repairability improvements with greater component modularity and easier access to internal components, the HomeView put up a fight nearly all the way through.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, iFixit’s teardown of the new Apple HomeView is now up, revealing a device that seems nearly impossible to take apart and repair. Watch it below.

Following last week’s launch of the Apple HomeView, iFixit today published its teardown of the device.

Contrary to recent teardowns, which found significant repairability improvements with greater component modularity and easier access to internal components, the HomeView put up a fight nearly all the way through.

With heavily glued or adhesive-bonded components, including the display, speakers, antennas, and logic board, the teardown proved particularly challenging, even after the adhesive securing the display’s speakers was soaked in isopropyl alcohol.

At one point, one of them broke apart during removal, while the logic board required considerable force to separate from the chassis due to the thermal adhesive holding it in place.

iFixit’s teardown covered the two HomeView variants: the tabletop model and the wall-mounted version. Interestingly, there are some internal differences between them, as the wall-mounted model has a slightly wider logic board to accommodate capacitors that are housed in the base of the tabletop version.

As a result, the wall-mounted HomeView also has smaller internal speakers, which helps explain the differences in their audio systems that Apple had already acknowledged at launch.

Back to the tabletop model, iFixit’s teardown also indicated that separating the display from the base requires either specialized tools or extensive, potentially destructive disassembly of the display assembly, thanks to the way Apple routed the connecting cables through the pivot mechanism.

Once iFixit was in the base, however, there was some good news: the USB-C port is modular and relatively easy to access, as are the passive radiators and the board powering the lower assembly.

Still, an extremely short cable connecting the woofer to the board underneath made disassembly difficult, with iFixit questioning how anyone would be able to reconnect it during reassembly.

Sources indicate that percentage of Apple owners who are interested in repairing their device. 0.000001%.

Percentage of Apple owners who will actually try and repair their device. 0.00000001%.

Given all these repairability challenges, Shahram Mokhtari joked that while iFixit doesn’t have an official repairability scorecard for this category of device, he would give the Apple HomeView a “BEEP this thing” out of 10.

  • In a latest interview, the Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother director reveals why he decided not to helm the superhero movie.
  • “Life’s too short to make shit films, so that was my significant lesson: I have to have full control over my script,” Tariq told The New Arab.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bassam Tariq was once attached to direct Marvel’s Blade with Mahershala Ali, but eventually exited the project.

In a latest interview, the Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother director reveals why he decided not to helm the superhero movie.

“Life’s too short to make shit films, so that was my significant lesson: I have to have full control over my script,” Tariq told The New Arab. “If we disagree, it’s between them and me. It’s quite sad because we had such high hopes for what we wanted to build.”.

Recent findings suggest that tariq told the publication that he found it “funny and strange to start casting and building without a proper script.” What complicated things is trying to explain to actors who their characters and didn’t want to disappoint them if they didn’t live up to the expectations. Watch on Deadline.

In a recent development, “That’s also very dangerous because if the text comes and it doesn’t add up to what you were saying, your credibility gets completely shot. All I have is my integrity, and I’ve been thinking about that a lot,” he added. “If you’re the bearer of bad news to your actors, but you’re not the one making any of these decisions — and it’s actually coming from a corporate entity — that’s not a great way to be a director. I know some people can take that and run with it, but I learned I was losing credibility with my actors, and it wasn’t a healthy way to operate as a filmmaker.”.

The silver lining in walking away from Blade and the film never getting made was that some of the costumes for Blade were eventually repurposed for Sinners.

In a recent development, “That was awesome. I was so happy that that’s the film we got out of it, because Sinners feels so much bolder than what we could have accomplished. Also, it felt so singular for Ryan Coogler, who has been building all these IPs for other people,” Tariq said. “Now he’s doing his own in such an unapologetically beautiful way, celebrating so many different facets of blackness, being an immigrant and the transcendence of music.”.

Although Tariq didn’t direct Ali in the Blade adaptation, they finally worked together on Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother.

“I’m blessed that Mahershala came along on this journey with me. The fights, I didn’t expect him to nail it on the first try. I think it was unexpected for him too, since he’d never done it before,” Tariq said. “What really blew me away was how he conducted himself with other actors. Sometimes actors can get greedy and want to make sure they give their best performance when the cameras are on them, and not be present when they aren’t.”.

Donald Trump has returned from his trip to Asia, and in a press briefing before a White House press corps eager to learn what had taken place in his closed door summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, as well as Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the president gleefully referred to as “my friend” this week in front of a room full of cameras.

So who can he speak for? Himself, of course, and the autocratic rulers like Putin whom he considered his close personal friends.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Amazon's Black Friday sale kicked off today, which means it's a good time to score some of the year's best prices on e-readers. Timing your purchase is now a bigger deal than ever (so to speak), as Amazon recently raised the price of basically every Kindle by $50 or more due to the ongoing RAM crisis.

Because of this, the prices aren't nearly as low as they were last year, but now is still the time to get a decent discount on a Kindle Paperwhite or Colorsoft—but if you'd rather read differently, you can also save big on a few worthy Kindle alternatives. Here are your e-reader best bets in the lead-up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

According to recent reports, the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people. An upgraded version of the basic Kindle, the Paperwhite adds a larger screen, temperature-adjustable lighting, water resistance, and better battery life—and if you opt for the Signature Edition, you also get double the storage and no lock screen ads. Earlier this year, it jumped in price to $250, even before the company introduced a fresh model—but you can get the 2024 model for $179.99, 28% off the new list price.

If you want a great Kindle but you don't care about paying extra for more storage or getting rid of lock screen ads, the non-Signature Edition of the Kindle Paperwhite is also a great buy right now. The 2024 model has been discounted to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. It's available in standard black, Jade, or Raspberry colors.

If you don't need the bells and whistles of the Paperwhite, you can also pick up the standard Kindle. It's still a very capable device, with good lighting, 16GB of onboard storage, and the ability to hook up your Bluetooth speakers to listen to Audible audiobooks. The standard Kindle, which now retails for $150, is marked down to $119.99, making it the cheapest Kindle option. Though I think it makes more sense to spend $10 more on the Signature Edition, this is the way to go if you want the cute Matcha color.

According to recent reports, if you like to read comics or you just appreciate looking at your book covers in full color, the 2024 Kindle Colorsoft is also at a strong 41% discount for Black Friday, bringing it down to around $170. For $10 less than the Paperwhite Signature edition, you get all the same perks (including an ad-free experience) and a color e-ink screen that's great for reading magazines, graphic novels, and manga. Color e-ink isn't for everyone, but if it's for you, the Colorsoft has the best color screen on the market. For an extra $10, the Colorsoft Kids Edition adds a case, a yearlong subscription to Kindle Kids+, and an extended warranty.

If you're looking for a combination e-reader and e-notebook, the Kindle Scribe is a great option. With a larger screen than Amazon's other e-readers, it offers all the benefits of the Paperwhite but adds support for the excellent Premium Pen stylus, allowing you to take notes in your Amazon e-books or create handwritten documents that you can later convert to text using the onboard AI tools. The 32GB black-and-white version of the Kindle Scribe is presently $349.99, while the Colorsoft version will run you $449.99. Both of these are the newest models, released in 2025.

It has been revealed that the new Kindle Scribe Colorsoft has all the same great features of the black-and-white version discussed above, but adds a full-color e-ink display. Combined with the large 11-inch screen, this makes it a great device for reading comics or magazine articles as they were meant to be read, or marking up PDFs using the included Premium Pen. This device usually costs a hefty $630, but the current Black Friday sale cuts $180 off of that price.

If you want to step outside of the Amazon ecosystem, the Kobo Libra Colour is a good bet. Discounted $30 to $229.99 at Best Buy, it's currently pricier than the Kindle Colorsoft, but you get a bit more for your money. While most of the specs are similar (they both use the same Kaleido 3 screen and offer 32GB of storage), the Kobo supports a stylus, so you can jot down notes in your books or keep a digital journal. It also has physical page-turn buttons, which the Colorsoft lacks.

If you don't want to be tied to the Amazon ecosystem and/or you're looking for a device that's a bit more portable, consider the Viwoods AiPaper Reader, presently marked down to $200, its lowest price ever. It's got a 6.13-inch screen, so it's the same size and shape as your phone, and it has a crisp e-ink screen with a strong (if not temperature-adjustable) front light and 128GB of onboard storage. The best part is, it runs on an open Android system, so you can install multiple reading apps, including Kindle, Nook, Kobo, and Libby, and keep all of your books in one place. (Check out my review of the Viwoods AiPaper Reader for more—it's a nifty little device.).

If you don't have a large Kindle library, you're moderately tech-savvy, and you praise portability above all else, I can't recommend Xteink's line of e-readers more highly. The 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic is at its lowest price ever, coming in at just under $55, around $34 off the list price. Meanwhile, the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 is about a dollar more; that's a less-generous 19% discount. I own both, and while the Classic is definitely worth the current sale price, I actually prefer the form factor of the smaller X3 (presently $55.72), which is about the size of a library card.

If you're feeling tentative about trusting a seemingly no-name Chinese tech brand, read more about the devices in my review, or listen to the collected wisdom of the tens of thousands of people in the bustling r/xteink Reddit group.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Industry observers note that follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

According to recent reports, no. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

In a upcoming post published on its developer portal, Apple today confirmed a series of changes to App Store pricing, as well as updates to tax rules affecting developers and customers in several countries, including the US.

According to the company, developers’ proceeds from eligible app and In-App Purchase sales have been adjusted in four countries, reflecting the following tax updates:.

Specific to Botswana and Rwanda, Apple said that “Exhibit B of the Paid Applications Agreement will be updated to indicate that Apple collects and remits applicable taxes.”.

Developers can review and update their tax category selections in App Store Connect.

Additionally, starting December 3, developers who rely on Apple’s automatic pricing adjustments will see changes to app and In-App Purchase prices in:.

Apple usually makes these adjustments to account for changes in taxes and foreign exchange rates, and notes that prices won’t change in countries selected as the base storefront, for auto-renewable subscriptions, or in storefronts where developers manually manage their prices.

Finally, starting January 1, 2027, apps and In-App Purchases in the SaaS, App Store Software, Software Training Material, Dating, and Boosting categories will become subject to sales and use taxes in California.

Apple noted that “prices on the United States storefront are displayed to customers exclusive of taxes, so the tax change will not affect them,” but added that while developers’ proceeds will remain unchanged, “the total amount customers are charged, inclusive of tax, may increase.”.

And while both the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are excellent devices in their own right, they can be pretty pricey (particularly the Ultra). That's why the third category, the SE, is actually best for most people, and Lifehacker's choice for best smartwatch gift of the year. Better yet, the third-generation SE is currently $50 off ahead of Black Friday, perfect for most people asking for an Apple Watch this year.

Sources indicate that the SE 3 does just about everything you'd expect an Apple Watch to do. It, of course, has a heart rate sensor to keep tabs on your pulse, including high and low heart rate alerts; the ability to track dozens of different workouts and exercise types (including swimming, thanks to the device's water resistance); a sleep tracker with daily analyses available in the Health app; notification forwarding to check in on your alerts without opening your iPhone; and the ability to send and receive text messages.

It comes in two sizes (40mm and 44mm) depending on how large or small you prefer your watch. No matter which model you get, the watch comes with the S10 chip, Apple's last-generation watch processor. While it isn't as fast as the current S11 chip, the S10 is more than capable of running watchOS 27. Apple notes the SE 3 can run for up to 18 hours on a single charge, and up to 32 hours in Low Power Mode, with fast charging from 0% to 80% in 45 minutes.

The majority of the features missing from the SE 3 aren't essential. Apple's other watches have things like bigger, brighter displays, additional health tracking tools like hypertension alerts and an ECG sensor, longer battery life, and Audio Intelligence—the latter of which might be a benefit to miss, depending on who you are.

Industry observers note that if your giftee wants or needs any of those additional features, Series 12 or Ultra 4 might be a better choice. But for anyone who wants the essential Apple Watch experience, the SE 3 is simply the best-value watch Apple sells right now—especially at this discount. Right now, the watch starts at $199 for the 40mm watch, or $229 for the 44mm. You can also save on the cellular versions of these watches: $249 for the cellular 40mm watch, and $279 for the cellular 44mm model.

A set of major tech outages in close succession is leading some to speculate that they are connected, and that the US is under systemic attack by a hostile state.

All the evidence suggests otherwise, with individual explanations for each of them – and the White House is now saying as much in a bid to put fears to rest ….

Whether there was or wasn't a cyber attack, I wouldn't believe a single word from the White House.

Sources indicate that on Thursday, a widespread Microsoft 365 outage ran into the following day when two unrelated challenges coincided. Friday saw a nationwide ground stop of US air traffic due to a communication concern affecting all air traffic control centers. On Monday, a bug in a Chase bank system saw disruption not only to the bank itself, but also other banks where Chase was a party to a transaction. Finally, yesterday saw many Apple services offline, with retail stores also affected.

The Apple outage doesn’t appear to have been significant enough to have reached the administration’s radar, but CBS News reports secretary of state Marco Rubio saying the others are unrelated.

“The Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA. The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago. These challenges that we’ve seen from a technical standpoint are completely unrelated one from another,” Rubio noted […].

“We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind. Each of them are distinct, and they’re different in their causation.”.

The statement was backed by Senator Mark Warner.

Sources indicate that democratic Sen. Mark Warner, vice chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, also said on Tuesday that there’s no indication these incidents are the result of an attack.

Warner went on to say that the ability of AI systems to find vulnerabilities at “unprecedented speed” does, however, mean companies and government agencies alike need to be ready to patch vulnerabilities immediately.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday sales officially start Friday, November 28, and run through Cyber Monday, November 30, 2026, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before it's over.

It's Cyber Monday, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before the sales are over.

Sales are accurate at the time of publication, but prices and inventory are always subject to change.

Not every Black Friday or Cyber Monday deal is as sweet as it seems. With electronics and tech in particular, you could be buying last year's model that has actually been on sale since the summer—and was maybe a better price a few months ago. Here’s how to avoid impulse buying a misleading Black Friday “deal” and make sure you’re getting the best bang for your buck.

According to recent reports, when you see products like food, clothes, or home goods with a significant "Black Friday" or "Cyber Monday" tag slapped on them, it's probably safe to take advantage of that deal. Chances are it's the same exact product you'd find on other days of the year. The same can’t be said for a TV, laptop, and other tech deals, where the product itself is constantly being upgraded.

Because tech is always evolving, and retailers want to move inventory before upcoming models come out, electronics are especially susceptible to a practice known as "price anchoring." That's when retailers mark up prices in the weeks leading up to Black Friday, before "slashing" those prices back down, giving the appearance of a deal that isn't really a deal at all. Still, when you see that marked-up number, aka the "price anchor," you might get tricked into thinking you're saving money when you're not. There's also the false sense of urgency that gets created. It's second nature to assume that anything labeled "deal" won’t last long—even when this so-called deal price has actually been going on since the summer.

Price anchoring isn't even unique to Black Friday. The nonprofit Consumers’ Checkbook tracked prices at 25 major retailers over 33 weeks in 2022 and found that more than half the items tracked were offered at false discounts every week or almost every week. Less common, but also worth noting, is a known practice of "derivative" or retailer-exclusive models produced specifically for the holiday shopping season. These versions often feature cheaper components, fewer features, or lower specifications than their regular counterparts. A 55-inch TV from a reputable brand might look identical to the year-round model, but it could have a lower refresh rate, inferior panel technology, or fewer HDMI ports.

In a recent development, in the same vein, that "amazing deal" on a laptop might come with last year's processor, or a smartphone that's about to be replaced. The issue isn't that the tech is an older model, but again, it's that it probably has been at this low a price, or lower, since the summer. Alternatively, some deeply discounted electronics are refurbished units or open-box returns that have been repackaged. Again, while this isn't necessarily a bad thing, impulse buyers may not fully realize what they're buying.

The key phrasing here is impulse buying. Events like Black Friday are psychologically engineered to trigger impulse purchases. Limited-time offers, countdown clocks, and "while supplies last" warnings create artificial urgency. When you're caught up in the moment, it's easy to convince yourself you need a fresh tablet, smartwatch, or gaming console, even if you hadn't considered buying one before.

According to recent reports, to avoid a low-key scam, do your research. The easiest way to tell that you’re getting the correct product is by checking the model or serial number. And with online shopping, finding and double-checking those numbers is quick and easy. In addition, don't just compare prices—compare specs. Look at processor speeds, RAM, storage capacity, screen resolution, refresh rates, and connectivity options. A $300 laptop isn't a deal if a slightly more expensive model offers significantly better performance that will last longer.

Industry observers note that if you do see a deal that catches your eye, it could pay to wait. Cyber Monday, post-Christmas sales, and even January clearances often feature electronics deals that rival or beat Black Friday prices, all without the famous chaos and pressure. Then again, you risk more “out-of-stock” results if you wait, so the risk is up to you, depending on the popularity of the item you’re eyeing (and how badly you want it).

The bottom line: Don’t fall victim to a falsely advertised lower-quality product, and do a little research to find actually good deals ahead of time.

The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. It has been revealed that after launching Moonlock for Mac last year, MacPaw is bringing its scam-detection app to iPhone today. Here are the details.

When MacPaw introduced Moonlock on the Mac, the organization described its latest app as something that “complements Apple’s built-in security tools, protects from Mac-specific malware, and helps you understand cybersecurity better.”.

In practice, the Mac app includes real-time protection against potential threats. Consumers can also manually scan their Mac for malware, including suspicious files hidden in system folders and email attachments.

Beyond that, Moonlock includes a VPN to encrypt internet traffic, a network inspector that shows where apps are sending data and lets users block connections to specific countries, and an AI-powered scam detector that analyzes messages pasted into the app for signs of phishing. It also helps users review and adjust macOS security settings.

Today, MacPaw is launching Moonlock for iPhone, a move the firm notes “helps people recognize potential scams, understand their iPhone’s security and take practical steps to improve it.”.

In a recent development, unlike the Mac version, Moonlock for iPhone doesn’t scan for malware, as iOS prevents third-party apps from accessing other apps and their files. Instead, it focuses on identifying potential scams, checking for exposed personal information, and helping people improve their iPhone’s security.

On the iPhone, Moonlock lets consumers quickly check suspicious texts, screenshots, and QR codes for phishing, in addition to checking whether their email addresses have appeared in known data breaches.

As MacPaw explains it, Moonlock’s Scam Detect “helps people check suspicious messages they encounter throughout the day. Whether it’s a text message, a screenshot shared by a friend, or a QR code, customers can paste, scan or share content directly with Moonlock and receive an assessment explaining why something may be suspicious.”.

Here’s Oleg Stukalenko, Head of Product Management at Moonlock by MacPaw, on today’s launch:.

In a recent development, “When we launched Moonlock, our goal was to make cybersecurity something anyone could understand and use. But so much of what people do today, from banking to everyday conversations, happens on their phones. Bringing Moonlock to iPhone felt like the natural next step. We want to help people spot a scam before they tap, see where their security stands, and know exactly what to do next.”.

MacPaw adds that Moonlock for iPhone also includes the following features:.

MacPaw’s Moonlock for iPhone is free to download, with subscriptions available for $9.99 per month or $49.99 per year.

Head to Amazon.com in your web browser.

Hover over the Accounts & Lists menu on the top-right of the window, then select the Prime Membership option.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

Note that Amazon requires a bunch of clicks to finalize your cancellation, giving you lots of “opportunities” to change your mind.

Open the Amazon Shopping app on your mobile device.

Click the three horizontal lines on the bottom right.

Under Shop by Category, select Prime.

On the top bar, slide all the way to the end and select Help.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

As mentioned, closing your account will immediately end your access. Amazon also offers you the option to pause your benefits and billing temporarily instead of canceling them completely. Either way, your Amazon account is still active—you simply won’t have Prime benefits.

Finally, if you have other subscriptions connected to your Prime account, those will end when your billing is up. And if you signed up for Prime through the Android mobile shopping app or the Prime Video Android app, you’ll have to go through Google Subscription to manage your membership.

Its intelligent AI sensing algorithm drastically improves reliability by reducing false triggers caused by environmental factors like pets, airflow, and robotic vacuums. A built-in ambient light sensor also helps trigger smart home scenes based on both human activity and lighting conditions.

You might initially struggle to spot the new products in the company’s new releases section on its Amazon store. That’s because instead of each having its own section, you need to click or tap on the product in the top image.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the world has been waiting to play Grand Theft Auto VI, and the video game is finally here. Music, of course, is integral to all of it. There’s a soundtrack full of stars — the 34-track release, which is out today, features Travis Scott, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Arca, and more. In addition to that, there is a massive one-day festival inspired by the game, taking place in Miami on Nov. 21, with headliners Cardi B, Metro Boomin, and Justice, who also put together the game’s score.

Once you start playing, there’s even more music to discover through the game’s radio stations and celebrity DJ hosts. Here are some of the best music moments and surprise cameos from the biggest video game of the year.

It has been revealed that the game is full of celebrity guest DJs, which Rockstar began sharing a few weeks back. There’s Cocoteo FM hosted by Bad Bunny and RaiNao, Back Country Radio hosted by Morgan Wallen and Lana Del Rey, and Radio La Ola with Gloria and Emilio Estefan, plus tons more. But one that may surprise people is Stockyard FM, featuring two DJs named Victoria and Harrison — better known as PinkPantheress and the Dare. Victoria and Harrison are their real names, and their radio station is dedicated to experimental, left-of-center pop, electronica, and indie sleaze.

Recent findings suggest that one of the GTA VI radio stations, Radio La Ola, plays homage to Latin classics from over the decades. But one hugely surprising one is “Sopa de Caracol,” a massive but somewhat forgotten hit from the Nineties by Honduran band Banda Blanca. The inclusion made headlines in Central America, with the lead singer Pilo Tejada saying he was honored to have his voice reach new parts of the world.

Psych-rock band King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard is featured on the soundtrack: They’re one of several artists on the collaboration “Flower in a Hurricane,” which also earned them their first Billboard 100 entry. But that’s not the only place you can find them: Gizz fans noticed that throughout several parts of the game, you can hear snippets of what appear to be demos from the band, woven into the score. On Reddit, diehards have been pointing these out and playing guessing games as they wonder what projects these might be from.

Recent findings suggest that we’ve known that the French electronic duo Justice composed the original score for the game, but the official album won’t be out until Dec. 11. We’re getting to hear some of what they came up with the release of the game but there’s still more to come, including an anticipated collaboration with the Weeknd. The duo have since said this is the “first and last” video game they’ll ever score.

The soundtrack, which dropped on Nov. 19, is packed, featuring 34 songs by some surprising artists and stars. There’s newly introduced music from Travis Scott, the Fuerza Regida track “Suzuki,” which is charting in 15 countries, and there are also songs from Keith Richards, Kali Uchis and Helado Negro, and more. A lot of the music was inspired directly by Miami, which you can hear in new tracks from artists like JT.

Artists are getting into the game, too. Tinashe delighted fans with a hilarious livestream playing for the first time. The stream captured her making an epic getaway by flying an airplane and hysterically crashing it into the ground, then running out of ammo in a shootout. “I have no bullets!” she screams. “Holy shit, I’m going to have to beat the fuck out of them myself.” After several days of sold-out shows in the U.K., Noah Kahan stayed up late and wreaked havoc in Vice City while his wife was asleep.

Industry observers note that the world lost D’Angelo back in 2025, but his legacy lives on in Vice City. GTA VI players discovered that an unreleased track called “Kamakazi,” as confirmed by D’Angelo collaborator DJ Dojah, is one of the songs you can hear on the radio station Worldwide FM. D’Angelo’s “Lady” also plays on the in-game Honey FM channel, which is hosted by Chilli and T-Boz of TLC.

Recent findings suggest that while the creators of the game spent a ton of time adding interesting radio stations and track to the GTA VI universe, there is plenty of love for pop stars and major pop hits. Dua Lipa appears on the soundtrack, but the radio stations also feature plenty of pop girlies: There’s Chappell Roan’s “Hot To Go!,” Charli XCX’s “Good Ones,” and Addison Rae’s “Fame Is a Gun,” just to name a few, which players can blast while driving through Vice City.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

VWFNDR + MBL, an Android camera app that doesn’t overprocess and delivers high-quality DNG (RAW) files, is getting a 2.0 release with improved color grading and an expansion to the iPhone.

Sources indicate that VWFNDR + MBL introduced on Android in May 2026 with a few points that stood out. A unique UI that adapts to the shot, minimal processing for a natural look, and support for DNG files at a level that only Google’s Pixel Camera app can truly compete with.

The app has been downloaded over 300,000 times since then, and is now getting a pretty substantial update.

On Android, this comes in the form of new color grading profiles built into the app. “NATURAL,” “NIHON,” or “B+W.” The app still saves an unprocessed DNG alongside the JPG and the grading adapts across the frame rather than having a fixed result, keeping highlights and shadows in place.

Colour grades: MBL still records unprocessed Bayer RAW DNG, and the JPG it renders alongside now uses one of three grades: NATURAL, NIHON, or B+W. Grading happens on VWFNDR’s own spatial engine. Instead of applying a fixed LUT, it adapts across the frame, much like a raw editor, so highlights and shadows keep their detail. The DNG stays untouched.

Here’s what the output looks like:.

The rest of VWFNDR + MBL 2.0 takes place off of Android.

Industry observers note that in a rare case of the tables turning, MBL was released first on Android, and only on Android for the first several months. But VWFNDR is now bringing the app to iPhone with support for variable aperture on iPhone 18 Pro and Content Credentials, Apple’s version of the C2PA standard that’s meant to prove a photo is real and not AI-generated.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Quite frankly, the Hyundai Ioniq 9 gets a bad rap for the way it looks.
  • Recent findings suggest that that’s why I drove the Hyundai Ioniq 9 Calligraphy Design for the second time this year — just to convince myself that there are better 3-row midsize SUVs out there.
  • But after another week behind the wheel, I can tell you firsthand that judging the Ioniq 9 by its cover is a mistake.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Quite frankly, the Hyundai Ioniq 9 gets a bad rap for the way it looks. In fact, I stated in my 2026 Hyundai Ioniq 9 review that the design is an “odd mashup featuring a curvy front bumper with an even stranger-looking arched rear.” It’s one of the last SUVs I’d expect to win any beauty awards.

Recent findings suggest that that’s why I drove the Hyundai Ioniq 9 Calligraphy Design for the second time this year — just to convince myself that there are better 3-row midsize SUVs out there. I’ve spent more time testing 3-row SUVs than any other vehicle type this year, with models like the Kia Telluride, Volvo XC90, Volkswagen Atlas, and Lucid Gravity getting my seal of approval.

But after another week behind the wheel, I can tell you firsthand that judging the Ioniq 9 by its cover is a mistake. Here’s what I realized.

Best long distance driving efficiency.

Best short distance driving efficiency.

Industry observers note that as with most vehicles, fuel economy and efficiency tend to dwindle over time — which is why I’m shocked that the Ioniq 9 is an exception. I was already impressed by the 3 mi/kWh average I got when I drove it last year, yet my second run delivered even better results.

In a recent development, across 130.5 miles of mixed driving, my second go-around with the Ioniq 9 yielded an impressive 3.3 mi/kWh. What surprised me even more was the substantial improvement in city driving, where I recorded a peak tally of 4.5 mi/kWh — up from my previous best of 3.8 mi/kWh.

In a recent development, considering it’s marketed as a three-row family hauler, it’s remarkable that the Ioniq 9 can post numbers like this. That extra efficiency is critical, too: while this trim carries an EPA-estimated range of 311 miles, averaging 3.3 mi/kWh puts its real-world range closer to 363 miles.

I’ll admit I was harsh on the Hyundai Ioniq 9’s styling the first time around. While it certainly takes cues from the subcompact Hyundai Kona, I argued that it was an odd mashup that was confused about what aesthetic it was trying to go after.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

After spending another week with it, though, its unconventional look slowly grew on me — even if that appreciation is mostly isolated to the front of the EV. That’s due to Hyundai’s signature Parametric Pixel LED light bar, which stretches across the nose like something straight out of a sci-fi movie. Those individual blocks give it a retro look that becomes even more dazzling from dusk into the night. In a sea of generic crossovers, this one certainly commands road presence.

That said, I still haven’t come to terms with the back half of this electric SUV. That tapered, upright rear end remains the hardest pill to swallow, giving it the look of a boat tail. Despite this, I now appreciate that the shape is doing the heavy lifting to make it aerodynamic — and subsequently boosting its efficiency.

Recent findings suggest that whether I’m making a quick stop at the local grocery store or on my 30+ mile commute to work, the 2026 Hyundai Ioniq 9 doesn’t skimp on the comforts. Step inside, and it’s clear Hyundai prioritized first-class comfort for the people riding up front and in the middle.

For example, the plush H-Tex seats strike a great balance of softness and support — which, for the driver, includes extra pampering courtesy of Hyundai’s Ergo Motion seat. When activated, it slowly adjusts the firmness of the cushion, sort of like getting a mini massage while driving, all to deter fatigue on longer hauls.

Sources indicate that still, the real VIP treatment belongs to the second-row captain’s chairs. With both heating and ventilation, plus power-reclining backrests and extendable footrests, they turn the middle row into a rolling lounge. However, the third row leaves more to be desired. Although I still appreciate having the extra seating capacity in a pinch, the legroom back there is practically nonexistent for adults — so I’d much rather keep that rear bench folded flat to make way for more trunk space.

At nearly $80,000 as tested, the Ioniq 9 Calligraphy Design comes loaded with just about every luxury and tech perk anyone could ask for — and rightfully so.

​I still absolutely love Hyundai's adaptive cruise control, which makes long drives bearable and includes a dedicated lane-centering button on the steering wheel that also happens to work on local roads. Adding to that is a crisp Head-Up Display that projects my speed and navigation right onto the windshield.

​Changing lanes is effortless thanks to the Blind-Spot View Monitor (which streams a live camera feed straight into the digital gauge cluster) and a digital rearview mirror that offers a wider field of view than a conventional glass mirror.

​Back-seat passengers get plenty of love, too, with built-in rear side-window sunshades, a massive panoramic sunroof, and dazzling customizable ambient lighting that sets an upscale mood after dark.

​There’s also practical utility in the form of a handy 120V outlet accessible right in the trunk, letting me power laptops, tailgating gear, or small appliances straight off the SUV’s battery.

At nearly $80,000 as tested, the 2026 Hyundai Ioniq 9 Calligraphy Design is easily one of the most expensive vehicles in Hyundai’s entire lineup — and that price tag has long made me a skeptic.

Sources indicate that ​Yet spending a second week behind the wheel proved that judging it at face value is a mistake. Between its even better real-world efficiency, spacious cabin suited for families, and a laundry list of thoughtful luxury features, the Ioniq 9 delivers where it counts most: a family hauler that's rich in utility and backed by an efficient drive.

A massive AI correction wreaked more havoc on Wall Street, ending one of the worst weeks in recent memory for the stock market and erasing all of the Nasdaq‘s gains for the year.

About $4 trillion in market value was wiped out across the AI sector, with Sandisk, Micron, Seagate, Applied Digital, Broadcom, Nvidia, Dell, AMD and Meta all taking significant hits. The Nasdaq fell 1,261 points, or 5%, logging its seventh straight down day, the longest losing streak it has had since 2020.

In a recent development, the Dow and the S&P 500 fared a bit better, but still slipped 2% and 4%, respectively. Related Stories News Anthropic Shares End First Day Of Trading Up 17% In Volatile Session As AI Giant Goes Public News Utopai Studios Opens Beverly Hills Office, Targets 500 Production Jobs Globally In 2027.

Industry observers note that the selloff in tech coincided with two major developments in AI earlier in the week: Anthropic‘s IPO and a leadership change at Nvidia. Watch on Deadline.

In a recent development, after raising a record $81 billion in going public Thursday, Anthropic fell back near its $83 opening price mark. Earlier in the week, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, was ousted after admitting to multiple affairs, including one with a woman suspected by U.S. intelligence agencies of being a Chinese spy. The scandal is likely to disrupt the AI sector for some time due to pending investigations into the affair and also a complex web of investments making Nvidia not just the leading AI chipmaker but a key investor in many emerging companies.

Against the gloomy backdrop, core Hollywood companies fared slightly better, even if it wasn’t a banner day. Disney, Skydance and Netflix all shed between 2% and 4%. Comcast, buoyed by strong internet demand from Grand Theft Auto VI, finished up a fraction.

The reason why was that I treated AMT as a data problem - but in reality, the bottleneck is architecture. There are a lot of parellels that you can draw for OMR (first model i made) and AMT. both traditionally were tackled early on using algorithms. later, in both fields they plugged in giant LLM components. These models would naturally become overfit to synthetic data, since globally the problems of AMT and OMR become different than if you treat it locally. But, for both you can reframe it as a local problem. For OMR, using a detector model. For AMT, a pitch-lane model.

The changing of the clocks has taken its toll on my sleep this Fall. After long evenings bathed in artificial light, I've been feeling more wired than tired at bedtime. But thanks to one surprising gadget, lately I've been more consistent with my bedtime – and that's a good thing as studies link sleep consistency with better life expectancy.

Industry observers note that now that I’m prioritising a consistent sleep routine, I’m also waking up less through the night. So what is this surprising gadget? A red light face mask. Were you expecting something different? Mask aside, red light is said to accentuate the production of sleep hormones.

Sources indicate that however, sceptical that I’ve been lulling myself to sleep with nothing more than a placebo effect, I called on double-boarded sleep medicine specialist Dr. Chris Winter to ask whether the science around red lights sleep benefits checks out. Here's what he said...

Due to my job, I have a collection of gadgets to reach for when it comes to bedtime – the Ozlo Sleepbuds, Hatch Sleep Clock and the Oura Ring 5 included.

But one that's really surprised me lately is the Bob and Brad PhysioFace Light Therapy Mask, available for $169.99 (was $199.99) at Amazon.

I've been using the mask, chiefly marketed for skincare purposes, as part of my bedtime routine and it's helped me put down my phone and get to sleep on time.

As much as I love my Hatch clock, I don't love that I have to use my phone to alter settings. That's the beauty of this red light mask – it’s independent from my phone (there's no app to download) with control buttons attached to the device itself.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

That means I am actually making my bedroom a phone-free space and instead focusing on winding down for a great night's sleep.

It's hard to quantify exactly how well the red light mask is improving my sleep quality. But one thing is for sure: by the time I remove the mask, I feel sleepy and it never takes me long to dose off into a deep sleep.

According to my Garmin sleep timeline, I've reached deep sleep within half hour of dropping off, and continue to cycle through healthy sleep stages.

But what does Dr. Winter think? "It’s possible that taking a quiet break for your skincare routine is helping you unwind, particularly if it replaces scrolling or other stimulating activities.

"But feeling that you’re sleeping better doesn’t tell us whether the benefit is coming from the light itself, the routine, or something else.

"I would view it as a potentially relaxing part of your routine — not a proven sleep treatment," the board-certified neurologist cautions.

White and blue light from screens is bad news for sleep. But as the nights draw in, a lot of our evenings are powered by these types of light. This winter, I’ve been making a conscious effort to swap my overhead light for the sundown setting on my Hatch Sleep Clock. I've also been swapping doomscrolling with reading time while wearing my red light mask.

Sources indicate that 20 minutes prior to bedtime – after writing my do-to list for the following day and shutting off my phone for the night – I pop the mask on in bed and start reading a book. The 10-minute timer on the mask ensures I read for at least 10 minutes before drifting off.

In a recent development, the mask has three light modes with different colored lights. I've been using the BOOST mode that combines red light and near-infrared light. As well as supposedly boosting skin health, red light is associated with relaxation and there is some science associating it with improved sleep quality.

Although evidence is limited, research by Chinese scientists published in the National Library of Medicine, suggests red light influences melatonin secretion, improving sleep initiation.

Dr. Winter also referred to a 2026 review of five randomized trials that found a modest improvement in self-reported sleep quality when red light was introduced. "But the authors emphasized that the evidence was limited and imprecise," he notes.

Additionally, red light face masks, like my Bob and Brad model, are built to increase collagen production. They do this by penetrating the skin with red light, which stimulates the cells responsible for collagen synthesis. Besides improving skin elasticity, collagen can also improve sleep. A 2024 study concluded that increasing collagen at bedtime reduces sleep fragmentation.

Placebo or not, the mask has helped me prioritise a consistent bedtime routine over the past two weeks, and sleep better than I was immediately after the clock change.

Recent findings suggest that I’ve been writing about sleep for over two years, and one thing I’ve learnt is that your sleep routine must be personal. A gadget or habit that works for someone else may not work for you.

Sources indicate that if you’re struggling to sleep, you may need to try a few different methods or technologies before you hit on one that clicks. But one piece of advice sleep experts all agree on is that you need a relaxing prelude to sleep if you want to clock quality ZZZs.

A nighttime routine involves practising the same sequence of activities in the run up to your bedtime, helping prepare both your brain and body for sleep. In time, and with consistency, your body clock will come to recognise this routine as a signal to sleep, helping you drift off easily.

It has been revealed that dr. Winter explains: "A bedtime routine creates a predictable opportunity to step away from work, screens and other stimulating activities, rather than expecting your brain to switch off the moment your head hits the pillow. Pairing that wind-down period with a consistent sleep schedule and lower lighting helps support your body’s sleep-wake rhythm.".

This routine should be "simple, enjoyable and easy to repeat" and can include activity you find relaxing, be that a dark shower, mediation, reading, stretching or simply listening to calm music.

"You don’t need an elaborate checklist or expensive equipment—the goal is to wind down, not give yourself another assignment," advises the host of the Sleep Unplugged podcast.

"Think of the routine as making room for sleep, not forcing it to happen.".

With an impressive 4.5 stars from over 1,200 reviews, the iconic NEOM Wellbeing Pod is loved by many wellness fanatics from both sides of the Atlantic. Its designed to deliver the perfect amount of essential oils in minutes to create a calm haven in your bedroom. Catch it with 17% off now, bagging you a $24/£25 saving with free delivery included.

According to recent reports, the one for those who need total blackout to fall asleep, the SilkSound Sleep Mask is made with ultra-soft, skin-friendly silk, and laced with Bluetooth speakers to block out light and muffle unwanted sound. Our reviewer, Ruth Jones, rates the SilkSound as some of the best sleep headphones you can buy. At $34.99 now, it offers exceptional value for money, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Although The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is steeped with nostalgia for Hollywood’s past, David Fincher claims to represent the future.

While many have criticized the Quentin Tarantino-penned sequel to Once Upon a Time in Hollywood (2019) for the apparent onscreen use of Gen AI, the 3x Oscar-nominated director recently shared his thoughts on the rapidly growing tech.

“I’m not a Luddite, so I don’t fear the unknown,” Fincher told the Los Angeles Times.

“Is everyone satisfied that we have figured this art form out enough that what we really need to do is go back to celluloid?” he continued. “How long have people painted? 40,000 years? We’re talking about a thing that’s a hundred years old and everyone’s going, ‘Stop. Pencils down. No more iterating. It’s not necessary to have at your fingertips the ability to change the color of that person’s eyes.'” Watch on Deadline.

Fincher added, “Well, it exists. Should we not use it?”.

The comments come after several fans have taken to social media to criticize the apparent use of AI in the film as “astounding to an absurd degree,” with one viewer saying they “walked out of Cliff Booth completely gutted.”.

Set in 1977, eight years after Once Upon a Time…, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth follows Brad Pitt’s eponymous stuntman, now a projectionist who moonlights as a Hollywood fixer, getting caught up in a conspiracy that involves a Filipino gang and a stolen Oscar.

Premiering Thanksgiving on Imax, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth premieres Dec. 23 on Netflix.

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Aaron Pierre starred as John Stewart in the HBO & DC Studios series Lanterns and was set to play him across the DC Universe.
  • Sources indicate that however, with Peter Safran and James Gunn no longer co-heads of DC Studios, the future of the world they were building seems uncertain.
  • Recent findings suggest that “I haven’t had very much time at all to process the enormity of that news,” Pierre remarked on the November 19 episode of the IndieWire: Screen Talk podcast about finding out that day that Safran and Gunn were leaving DC Studios.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aaron Pierre starred as John Stewart in the HBO & DC Studios series Lanterns and was set to play him across the DC Universe.

Sources indicate that however, with Peter Safran and James Gunn no longer co-heads of DC Studios, the future of the world they were building seems uncertain. In a fresh interview, Pierre reacted to Safran and Gunn’s exits and shared his thoughts on what happens next.

Recent findings suggest that “I haven’t had very much time at all to process the enormity of that news,” Pierre remarked on the November 19 episode of the IndieWire: Screen Talk podcast about finding out that day that Safran and Gunn were leaving DC Studios. “But what I can say is that my relationship with James and my relationship with Peter is a beautiful relationship.”.

He continued, “I’ve really loved every moment, collaborating with them and working with them and getting to know them. And I’m excited to, beyond this point, in a different context, collaborate with them again. And I’m also excited to see what happens next for DC.” Watch on Deadline.

Pierre was to reprise his Lanterns role in Gunn’s Man of Tomorrow, which releases in theaters July 9, 2027. With the DC Studios head changing, it’s unknown what future they are planning and could eventually make edits to the Superman sequel to keep it contained.

RELATED: Skyler Gisondo On The Future Of ‘The People V. Gorilla Grodd’ After James Gunn’s DC Exit: “There’s A Lot Of Questions”.

The actor was asked if his character could possibly get edited out of the film, to which he mentioned, “I think for me, we did the film, and we really loved every moment of doing the film. And what happens beyond this point is not my decision. So I’m very at peace.”.

“I’m very at peace, and what will be will be,” he continued. “But what I do know is that those friendships will last beyond this point. And also those artistic, creative, working collaboration relationships will live beyond this point as well. And as I say, I’m excited to see where DC goes from here.”.

RELATED: ‘Constantine’ Director Feels “More Hopeful” For Sequel Following James Gunn & Peter Safran’s DC Studios Exit.

Recent findings suggest that amid the administration change at DC Studios following the Paramount and Warner Bros. merger, there has been a lot of speculation about Man of Tomorrow and the changes incoming executive Jeremy Latcham would make to the movie.

Gunn took to social media to debunk the rumors, posting on Threads, “No one from Skydance has even seen the movie – the only people that have are Peter Safran and a very small trusted group of friends and family. So any stories around this narrative are false.”.
